sections.heading: Devnet 8 (Platåberget) Launch
sections.summary: Devnet 8 launched hours before the call; Glamsterdam (Gloas) fork activation is scheduled for next Thursday at 7:50 UTC.
sections.body:
- Devnet 8, aka Platåberget, launched a few hours before the call and is currently running Fulu; Glamsterdam (Gloas) activation is set for next week Thursday at 7:50 AM UTC.
- Validators and builders who want to test the fork transition should make deposits or get onboarded before Gloas goes live.
- Links shared: [Forkcast devnet page](https://forkcast.org/devnets/glamsterdam-devnet-8/), [faucet](https://faucet.plataberget.ethpandaops.io), [Dora explorer](https://dora.glamsterdam-devnet-8.ethpandaops.io/).
- EthPandaOps blog post forthcoming, waiting for a few things to settle.

sections.heading: Final Gas Repricing Results
sections.summary: Gas repricing numbers for EIP-2780, EIP-8037, and EIP-8038 are confirmed final; no client code changes needed, and 200M gas limit is safe.
sections.body:
- Jochem presented final gas repricing results for EIP-2780, EIP-8037, and EIP-8038, confirming the numbers presented at ACD 90 are safe.
  - Acknowledged contributors: Maria (research/analysis), Kamil from Nethermind (gas benchmarks tool), Rafael (benchmarker tool), Luis (benchmarks), and all client teams for optimizing bottlenecks.
- The execution-spec-tests at version 8.1.0 are correct and final; no spec changes needed, so clients do not need to modify their code.
- 200 million gas can be safely supported at Glamsterdam — over 3× the current 16 million limit.
  - Safety anchor is approximately 75 Mgas/s, where all clients are clearly safe.
  - Toni noted that even 300M would have a safety buffer and suggested pushing for 300M right after Glamsterdam.

sections.heading: EIP-8261: Gas Limit Schedule via CL Config
sections.summary: CL clients broadly support EIP-8261 for scheduling gas limit increases post-fork; Nimbus expressed skeptical neutrality but no opposition since it is optional.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8261](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8261) introduces a new CL config parameter to hard-code a gas limit schedule (e.g., stepwise increase from 60M to 200M at specified epoch offsets after fork activation).
  - The flag is optional: clients may ignore it, and users can still override local gas limit values.
- This is purely a CL-side change; EL clients confirmed it does not affect them.
- Client support:
  - Prysm: approved and merged.
  - Lighthouse: approved the PR into consensus spec.
  - Lodestar: implemented; supports incremental gas limit pumping.
  - Teku: ready, PR being reviewed.
  - Nimbus (Dustin): "skeptical neutrality" — not convinced of the safety advantage of incremental staging, since there's not enough time between steps for redeployments, but since it's optional, no objection.
- Marius asked to stop spending time on it; nixo confirmed moving forward with the change.
- Nico noted that increasing blob limit gradually was helpful for catching performance regressions on mainnet that weren't visible on testnets.

sections.heading: History Expiry Readiness
sections.summary: Clients vary in history retention defaults (pre-merge to ~5 months); agreement to converge on a single number in the ETH R&D history expiry channel.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray raised the concern that 2TB node operators are hovering at 1.5–1.8 TB, and with EIP-8037 at 150M gas the expected state growth is ~120 GB/year, making history expiry necessary.
- Current client defaults:
  - Nethermind: stores history up to the merge; plans to drop to Dencun or more aggressively to ~6 months.
  - Erigon: stores last ~262,000 blocks by default (about 5 months), per EIP-8252.
  - Geth: has fork-minus-1 implemented and a PR for rolling expiry within the last 100K blocks.
  - Reth: no firm default yet but no objection to dropping more history.
  - Besu: currently only drops pre-merge blocks; team was fine with 33,024 epochs (~5 months) retention window but needs some implementation work.
  - Ethrex: still reviewing, will likely follow other clients.
- Ben Adams flagged that clients should coordinate to the same window, otherwise syncing history from peers becomes an issue if retention windows differ.
- Consensus to use a predictable time/block-based window rather than fork-minus-1, since fork intervals are unpredictable.
- Action: converge on a single number in the ETH R&D history expiry channel and decide where to spec it.
- EF is producing and serving [era files via torrents](https://ethresear.ch/t/torrents-and-eip-4444/19788); Parithosh confirmed this is ongoing.

sections.heading: Hegotá Timeline and PFI Process
sections.summary: PFI list should be finalized by next call; client preference lists due by September 10th; EIPs without a champion will not be merged into the Hegotá meta-EIP.
sections.body:
- The August 6th deadline for proposing PFI EIPs has passed; a large number came in last minute, totaling 17 proposals to present.
- Every PFI EIP needs a clear champion; if nobody can speak for an EIP on a call, it will not be merged into meta-EIP 8081 (Hegotá).
- No objections to having client preference lists ready by September 10th (two ACDE calls from now).
- Marius commented that he doesn't think any of the gas-repricing PFIs should be done in Hegotá; Rakita suggested TLOAD/TSTORE repricing might be worth doing differently.

sections.heading: EIP-7923, EIP-3298, and EIP-5920 Presentations
sections.summary: Jochem championed three EIPs: linear memory costing (report forthcoming), refund removal (agreement to focus on storage-clearing refund only), and PAY opcode (championed by Jochem).
sections.body:
- **[EIP-7923](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7923): Linear Page-Based Memory Costing** — Co-PFI'd with Charles Cooper (Vyper compiler).
  - Proposes removing the quadratic memory pricing introduced in Frontier; the quadratic bound is no longer needed because EIP-7825 (transaction gas limit cap, shipped in Fusaka) bounds memory allocation.
  - Jochem plans to update the spec to remove the memory cap implied by the current EIP, simplifying it, and to write a report on maximum allocatable EVM memory under linear pricing.
  - Report and updated spec to be delivered within two weeks or before next ACDE.
- **[EIP-3298](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-3298): Removal of Refunds** — Outdated EIP number but intent remains valid.
  - Currently only two refund sources remain: storage set from non-zero to zero, and EIP-7702 delegation (25,000 gas upfront, 12,500 refunded if account exists).
  - Rakita argued only the storage-clearing refund (original X → 0) should be removed, while the reset refund (A → B → A, reverting to original value) should stay.
  - Jochem agreed with this distinction; further discussion to happen async.
  - Simplifies EVM significantly; complicated interactions with cold data floor gas and max gas cap would be eliminated.
  - EIP-7778 (broadcast accounting without refunds) already partially deprecated refunds.
- **[EIP-5920](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-5920): PAY Opcode** — Jochem volunteered to champion.
  - Currently, sending ETH to an EOA without executing code requires the CREATE + SELFDESTRUCT pattern, which is expensive and targeted for removal via EIP-4758.
  - PAY opcode simplifies contract security audits by avoiding foreign code execution when transferring ETH.
  - lightclient noted that with log events on ETH transfers now in place, PAY is more acceptable.

sections.heading: EIP-8358 and EIP-8374: Net Gas Metering and Persistent Warm Access
sections.summary: Rakita presented two EIPs: net gas metering saves ~4K gas on repeated account changes in calls; persistent warm access across reverts simplifies access list handling.
sections.body:
- **[EIP-8358](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12058): Net Gas Metering for Account Changes**
  - Discounts gas when call target or callee was already changed earlier in the transaction, saving ~4K gas when both are changed.
  - Also affects minimum gas that must be sent to callees due to gas stipend calculations.
- **[EIP-8374](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12128): Persist Warm Access Sets Across Reverts**
  - Once an account or storage slot is loaded into the access list, it stays warm even if the call reverts.
  - Positioned as a small step toward cross-block access lists in the future.
  - Danno Ferrin raised concern that access list handling across reverts is historically one of the most finicky areas to implement and test, and warned this may be bigger than it looks, especially when supporting both pre- and post-fork behavior in the same binary.
  - Rakita responded that the EIP-7825 floor gas changes already cleared many edge cases, and the change is essentially skipping the journal entry for access list reverts.

sections.heading: EIP-8368: CPSB Recalibration for New Gas Limit
sections.summary: Simple recalibration of the EIP-8037 cost-per-state-byte constant needed for any gas limit increase; Toni presented on behalf of Maria.
sections.body:
- [EIP-8368](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8368) is a straightforward recalibration of the constant introduced in EIP-8037, which had its dynamic recalibration removed during Fusaka.
- Toni presented: if the gas limit is raised in Hegotá, this constant must be adjusted; it should be CFI'd in the meantime.
- Together with data repricing EIPs, this is one of the EIPs needed to push toward a 600 million gas limit.
- Marius expressed support in chat ("8368: good").
- Maria may present it in more detail at the next ACDE when she can attend.

sections.heading: EIP-8077 and EIP-8094: Transaction Announcement Metadata and Blob-Aware Mempool
sections.summary: EIP-8077 adds sender and nonce metadata to transaction announcements for smarter mempool logic; EIP-8094 may be folded into sparse block pool work.
sections.body:
- **[EIP-8094](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8094): Blob-Aware Mempool** — Goal is to avoid nasty traffic redistribution when blob fees spike.
  - ~90% overlap with sparse block pool machinery; Csaba is considering removing the EIP or focusing only on the delta. PFI'd to preserve the goal.
- **[EIP-8077](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8077): Announce Transactions with Nonce** — Adds metadata (sender, nonce, potentially fees) to transaction hash announcements.
  - Currently nodes only see hashes with type and size metadata; they must randomly pull transactions with no intelligence.
  - Adding sender + nonce enables smarter mempool decisions, important for scaling the public mempool and for frame transaction handling.
  - Toni: "bullish announce txs nonce... will help with the frame mempool."
  - Marius expressed support for 8077.
  - Csaba noted that for small transactions, metadata makes the announcement nearly as large as the transaction itself, so optimal design is size-dependent.
  - Barnabas asked about nonce size limits; Marius confirmed U64 (canonical nonce limit).

sections.heading: EIP-8355: ML-DSA Precompiles, EIP-8372: Normalized State Gas Limit, EIP-8375: eMBER, EIP-8219: Checked Arithmetic
sections.summary: Four additional PFIs presented: PQ signature precompiles using FIPS 204, state gas normalization for demand-responsive pricing, MEV burn via ePBS, and checked arithmetic opcodes.
sections.body:
- **[EIP-8355](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12048): ML-DSA Precompiles** ([slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1N9GLJNsPYF1Q_yXWQJnOKo0bADSZT2mSIZ-1pu1I-Ks/edit?slide=id.g3f6d86c03a1_0_0#slide=id.g3f6d86c03a1_0_0)) — Presented by Danno Ferrin.
  - Proposes precompiles for FIPS 204 ML-DSA verification at all three security levels (44, 65, 87), using compressed keys and full-width messages.
  - Every client language already has or will have ML-DSA built in by Hegotá ship date; clients should not write their own cryptography.
  - Diverges from prior EIP-8051 by sticking strictly with FIPS 204: compressed keys (2-4 KB vs 20 KB expanded), all security levels, and only FIPS hash functions.
  - Multiple security levels provide crypto-agility hedge if ML-DSA-44 is weakened by future cryptanalysis.
  - Kevaundray questioned the need for three precompiles; Danno argued not everyone is comfortable with level 2 security, and Google initially didn't even ship ML-DSA-44.
  - Arbitrum noted MAX_VERIFY_GAS is insufficient for DoS vector mitigation on L2s without an aggregation service.
- **[EIP-8372](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8372): Normalized State Gas Limit** — Presented by Anders Elowsson.
  - Addresses uncertainty about post-Glamsterdam state gas demand: if demand for state creation is too low or too high relative to execution, EIP-8037's max metering function creates suboptimal outcomes.
  - One-time fork-boundary calibration adds a constant to adjust cost per state byte while normalizing the state gas limit, measured in normalized units.
  - Simpler alternative to the previously proposed EIP-8075 (floating price).
- **[EIP-8375](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12130): eMBER** — Presented by Ben Adams.
  - Burns a percentage (~30%) of protocol-visible execution value to reduce security impact of large execution rewards.
  - Three components: universal priority fee burn, external builder burn target, and a PTC-observed floor from best public bids.
  - lightclient cautioned that ePBS usage should be observed in practice before building on top of it.
  - Terence warned this creates strong incentive for proposer-builder cartels to side-pay and avoid the burn.
- **[EIP-8219](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8219): Checked Arithmetic Opcodes** — Presented by Hubert Ritzdorf.
  - Introduces safe ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV opcodes that revert on overflow, replacing multi-opcode safe math patterns.
  - Solidity safe addition currently costs 79 gas; this would reduce it to ~5 gas equivalent and shrink bytecode significantly.
  - Alternative: single CHECKED opcode with a one-byte immediate selecting the operation, at the cost of less bytecode reduction.
  - Danno noted neither RISC-V nor WASM expose checked arithmetic, questioning whether the EVM should diverge from target architectures.
  - Jochem supported the concept, noting it's an opcode that should have existed since Frontier.

sections.heading: Frames / Native AA: Status, Client Positions, and L2 Concerns
sections.summary: Most EL clients support Frames (EIP-8141) for native AA; L2s (Arbitrum, Base) raised DoS and compatibility concerns; decision deferred to AA breakout on August 25th.
sections.body:
- Background: ACDE 233 (March) established consensus that native AA should be in Hegotá but did not lock in a specific implementation. Frames was CFI'd for Hegotá.
- **Client positions on Frames (EIP-8141):**
  - Geth: strongly championing Frames; lightclient emphasized significant iteration and concessions already made to get client support.
  - Nethermind: [now supports Frames](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2178#issuecomment-5223138367); Ben Adams would support it as headliner.
  - Besu: "not in opposition, happy to work on it."
  - Reth: taking no stance; Rakita is happy to work on it but defers decision to others.
  - Erigon (E3X): supportive.
  - Ethrex: supports Frames.
- **L2 concerns:**
  - Arbitrum (Offchain Labs): worried about throughput and DoS vectors; would need either a guarantor model (someone pays gas if tx reverts) or static verify frames to support 8141 on their L2.
  - Base (Chris): flagged EVM incompatibility — chains that don't hard fork Frames can't run it, risking wallets targeting two incompatible account standards. Proposed [EIP-8130](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8130) as alternative with explicit structural validation in the transaction type, key store system, and no new opcodes.
  - Tsahi (Offchain Labs): not opposed to 8141 in principle but has "big problems with 8141 as it's currently written," including concerns about L2 sequencers not profiting from block building and needing protection against invalid transactions.
- **Key technical debate:**
  - Felix (Geth) argued Frames allows L2 sequencers to impose arbitrary limits on acceptable transactions, reducing DoS risk. Also emphasized transaction assertions (post-conditions) as a critical Frames feature not present in 8130.
  - Chris argued 8130 satisfies the same long-term goals more performantly, with validation declared structurally in the transaction enabling fast-path cryptographic validation.
  - Derek Chiang noted an ongoing workstream to add static (pure function) validation to Frames, which would address L2 TPS/DoS concerns; Arbitrum confirmed static validation would solve their concern.
- **Process decision:**
  - Toni and others pushed for SFI + headliner status for Frames.
  - Ansgar urged sequential decisions: first lock in Frames as the specific AA variant, then discuss headliner status.
  - AA breakout calls restarting August 25th at 14:00 UTC; [agenda](https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2191).
  - Decision deferred to the AA breakout on August 25th, with the goal of bringing a conclusion to ACDE on August 27th.
  - lightclient: "I think we can find a version of 8141 that everyone is happy with. But if we keep arguing about major design differences, I think we will end up burning out and not changing anything."
  - lightclient committed to working with L2s to update Frames to address their concerns; Derek proposed incorporating L2 coauthorship.
